newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Rugby union-Benazzi promises French flair against Australia.
newsitem.headline: Rugby union-Benazzi promises French flair against Australia.

text.p: France captain Abdelatif Benazzi has promised to stay faithful to the running style that carried his side to the Five Nations championship in a two-test series against Australia later this month.

"It's most important to continue the style we played in the Five Nations - the French style - and run with the ball," Benazzi told reporters on Sunday after the tourists' first training session since arriving in Australia on Saturday.
France open their tour on Tuesday with a match against Victoria in the warm-up for the first test in Sydney on June 21. The second test will take place in Brisbane a week later.
The number eight said France also welcomed the opportunity to pit themselves against a different opponent after a tough European season.
"I get fed up playing against the same teams all the time," Benazzi said.
"We see how strong the Super 12 competition is and I want to compare French rugby with what you have in Australia."
The weak Victorian side, which lags far behind Queensland, New South Wales and ACT in playing strength, should present the tourists few problems.
Earlier, in Sydney, Australia coach Greg Smith moved Tim Horan across the backline to fill the problem flyhalf position for the first test.
Smith overlooked the claims of specialist flyhalfs David Knox and Scott Bowen.
Seven ACT Brumbies players, the biggest ever contingent from Canberra in a Wallaby line-up, won selection as a reward for reaching this season's Super 12 final.
The Brumbies, who lost to Auckland in the final, proved the surprise package of the tournament, overshadowing New South Wales and Queensland, Australia's traditional provincial powers.
Prop Ewen McKenzie, a key figure in ACT's success this season, was recalled after a two-year absence from test rugby.
